$comment: Where every identifier-shaped trigger comes from.
A trigger string is a factual claim about a published API in exactly the way
an import is: the router matches it against the added lines of a diff, so a
trigger that names an API nobody calls routes on nothing, silently, forever.
Nothing checked them until a routing-recall commit shipped three at once:
`registerdevicefornotifications` (the real API is
`registerDeviceForRemoteMessages`), `tobeintthedocument` (jest-dom's matcher,
misspelled; RNTL's is `toBeOnTheScreen`) and `layouttransition` (Reanimated's
is `LinearTransition`). All three were plausible. None of them existed.
Every trigger that is at least 8 characters and contains no space or hyphen
must appear as a key here. The value is either:
- a package name that has a COMPLETE export surface in
rn-lib-versions.json's `export_surfaces` — the guard then requires the
trigger to be a lowercase substring of one of that package's exports; or
- a string beginning with `!`, which is a written reason why the trigger
cannot be checked that way, and is skipped.
The `!` form is an escape hatch on purpose, and it is deliberately awkward:
you have to say out loud that the trigger is unverifiable and why. A guard
with no escape hatch gets deleted the first time it is inconvenient; this one
gets an honest line of prose instead. scripts/test.mjs asserts a floor on how
many triggers are genuinely checked, so the file cannot be quietly emptied
into reasons.
Adding a trigger without adding it here fails the build. That is the point.

triggers.gesturedetector: !react-native-gesture-handler; only spot-checked in verified_imports, no complete surface vendored
triggers.gesture.pan: !react-native-gesture-handler; Gesture.Pan() is a builder method on an export, not an export
triggers.useanimatedgesturehandler: !REMOVED in Reanimated 4; routed on deliberately so the agent can flag the migration, so absence from the current surface is the point
triggers.animated.view: !React Native core Animated (and Reanimated's default export); core has no vendored surface
